cohort: 361 women without previous vaginal births, attempting vaginal birth of a singleton fetus in breech presentation, between January 2015 and November 2021.
finding: When neonatal birthweight was >=3800 g, maternal BMI at birth and gestational diabetes were independently associated with an increased rate of intrapartum cesarean delivery, and maternal BMI at birth >=30 kg/m(2) was associated with a higher risk of neonatal acidosis.
mod_finding: Maternal BMI at birth and gestational diabetes were independently associated with a higher rate of intrapartum cesarean delivery among women attempting vaginal breech birth, particularly when neonatal birthweight was >=3800 g.
birth_weight: >=3800 g (as a specific condition for key findings)
